text: {"observations": "From 0.3 to about 4.4 s there are loud, noisy broadband bursts extending up to about 7 kHz, with energy concentrated below 1 kHz. These read as growls or snarl-roars rather than a pitched lion roar, which would show a strong low (about 200 Hz) harmonic stack with a rhythmic grunting series. From about 4.4 to 7.4 s there is weaker tonal material with slowly rising harmonic lines. From about 7.6 to 10 s there is a clean sustained harmonic tone: a fundamental near 500-600 Hz with harmonics around 1.1 kHz and 1.6 kHz, a sharp rising onset, then a steady pitch. This is typical of a howl. A sustained tonal howl at that pitch fits a wolf better than a lion or a bear, which roar in a lower and noisier way. A dog is possible, but a howl that is this long and steady following growls best fits a wolf. The answer is an inference from the howl-like ending rather than a certain identification.", "answer": "C"}
